hypothesis: A seven-pair portfolio using each pair's own 13/26/39 eligible-weekly-observation return direction, inverse-volatility risk weights and a 30% net USD-factor cap may generate positive executable risk-normalized returns after observed spread, commission, adverse slippage and swap-cost stress.
selection_rule: On discovery only, select the horizon with highest mean weekly net R after observed BID/ASK + $10 round-trip standard-lot commission + +1 pip adverse slippage + 2 pip-equivalent adverse swap per 7-day hold; tie-break by higher Holm-adjusted four-week block-bootstrap lower bound, then lower portfolio maximum drawdown. Confirmation does not choose a replacement horizon.
cost_model: Native observed BID/ASK executable sides; FundedNext official Stellar Forex commission $5/side/standard lot; assumed standard lot 100,000 units for normalized-R pre-screen, exact platform contract size not verified; extra slippage 0/0.5/1/2 pips per round trip; adverse swap proxy 2 pips/7-day hold primary and 4 pips/7-day stress, explicitly not the actual symbol swap.
falsification_gates: Preflight requires valid source hashes, timestamp integrity and exact cross-pair joins; no PnL before candidate-specific V2 preflight passes.
Every horizon requires >=200 eligible position legs and >=100 eligible weekly rebalance dates in discovery; >=100 legs and >=70 eligible dates in confirmation.
Primary-cost outcomes, if authorized, require net R > 0 and PF_R >= 1.05 in discovery and confirmation; stress-cost outcomes require net R > 0 and PF_R >= 1.00.
At least 2 of 3 complete discovery years 2018-2020 positive; no year contributes >70% of positive discovery net R.
Four-week block bootstrap, 10000 replicates, zero-trade weeks included; 95% lower bound >0 in discovery and confirmation; Holm adjustment across 3 discovery configurations.
note: Registered economic mechanism only. Current H1 source supports an exact T+60-minute bar-open proxy, not actual T+5-minute execution; actual contract size/swaps require verification before promotion.
